To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic administration of the glyco-lysis inhibitor iodoacetamide potentiates neuronal vulnerability to glutamatemediated neurotoxicity, and that pyruvatedependent energy metabolism might prevent glutamate-mediated neuronal death.
chronic inhibition of glycolysis in vivo potentiates glutamate-mediated neuronal toxicity and that pyruvated protects against neuronal damage induced by glutamate.

1) chronic systemic administration of iodoacetate, a glycolysis inhibitor, potentiates glutamate-mediated neuronal injury, 2) the neuroprotective effect of pyruvates is as efficient as that of MK-801, 3) the acute neuronal injury induced by local infusion of iodoacetates is associated with the accumulation of glutamate, taurine, and particularly aspartic acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic strategies to prevent neuronal damage induced by excitotoxic mechanisms.
the development of new neuroprotective strategies for cerebral ischemia/hypoxia/hypoglycermia.
the study of the role of glutamate and the excitatory amino acids in the mechanisms involved in the pathophysiology of ischemia/hypoxia and hypoglicemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition of glycolytic pathway, which is a major source of energy production in the brain, enhances glutamate-mediated neurodegeneration.
the glycolysis inhibition is able to potentiate the neurotoxicity of glutamate, but not the neurotoxic effect of aspartate.

inhibition of glucose oxidation in the brain facilitates glutamate-mediated neurodegenerative processes and that pyruvates might represent an efficient therapeutic tool in neurodegenerative disorders associated with ischemia or hypoglycemic episodes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extracellular accumulation per se of excitatory amino acid is not sufficient to cause neuronal damage.
inhibition of glucose oxidation in vivo is a necessary condition for the induction of glutamate-mediated neuronal lesions.
the excitotoxicity of glutamate is potentiated by a compromised energy metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of iodoacetate as a glycolysis inhibitor in the study of excitotoxicity is not recommended, since this compound induces neuronal damage in its own right.
inhibition of glycolysis can enhance neuronal damage in vivo.
the use of iodoacetate in in vitro studies might not be appropriate to mimic in vivo conditions.
